title: iPod Touch - Wikipedia
snippet:
The iPod Touch was the last product in Apple's iPod product line after the discontinuation of the iPod Nano and iPod Shuffle on July 27, 2017, after which Apple revised the storage and pricing for the iPod Touch with 32 and 128 GB of storage. On May 10, 2022, Apple discontinued the iPod Touch, effectively ending the iPod product line. The last iOS version to support the seventh-generation iPod Touch is iOS 15.

title: Here's where you can still buy an iPod touch - 9to5Mac
snippet:
While we don’t have exact inventory counts, here’s what we know is in stock. We’ll continue to update periodically as inventory changes.

## Apple

On Apple’s website, the iPod touch is completely sold out.

## Best Buy

Best Buy is sold out of all of the 32GB options with the exception of the Space Gray model. For 128GB, you can still buy a Blue and a Space Gray. Additionally, all of the 256GB models are out of stock. [...] ## Walmart

Walmart is where you’ll find some of the best prices for an iPod touch. 32GB is no longer available in Blue or (PRODUCT)RED. The 128GB is available in Space Gray and Pink. Walmart is entirely sold out of 256GB options as those seem to be the most popular models at many retailers.

## Amazon

The iPod touch is currently listed as a best seller on Amazon and there’s even a 5% discount on what’s available. The 32GB is available in Pink, Space Gray, and Gold. [...] Best Buy includes three months of Apple TV+, six months of Apple Music, and six months of Apple News+ for free when you purchase an iPod touch. Each subscription is for new subscribers only.

## Target

Target only has a 32GB option available for both the Blue and Space Gray models. Every other iPod touch is sold out.

For new subscribers, Target does offer four months of Apple Music for free through its Target Circle program.

title: Apple Has Officially Discontinued The iPod Nano And Shuffle, Reduces Price Of The iPod Touch
snippet: Previously, you had four configuration options for the iPod Touch: the 16GB model was priced at $199, 32 GB model was priced at $249, 64GB variant was priced at $299 and finally the 128GB variant was available for $399. To be exact, the price of the 32GB variant has been reduced by $50 while $100 have been reduced for the 128GB model. [...] Apart from Apple discontinuing the iPod Nano and iPod Shuffle, Apple has also adjusted the price of its iPod Touch with updated configuration. The company is now offering the iPod Touch in 32GB and 128GB configuration. The prior will cost you $199 while the latter is priced at $299 in the United States. Moreover, 32GB is the base line storage option for the iPod Touch now as the 16GB variant has been discontinued along with 64GB option. [...] The new configurations are available in stock at the moment on Apple's online store. Moreover, they are offered in the same color options as previously, that is Space Gray, Silver, Gold, Blue, Pink and Red. In addition to this, Apple updated the iPod Touch back in 2015, in which it updated the device's camera to 8-megapixel rear facing iSight camera and also incorporated the Apple A8 chip. You can get your hands on the iPod Touch from Apple's online store.

title: History of the iPod | Back Market
snippet:
on. The iPod touch continued to receive updates until May 2019, and in May 2022, Apple officially discontinued the last iPod standing. By the time it was discontinued, the iPod touch had gone through seven generations in its 12-year lifespan. And at its farewell party, one question remained: why was the iPod needed when it was now part of the iPhone? This marked the end of an era. | Gen 3 | September 2009 | 32 to 64 GB storage |
| Gen 4 | September 2010 | Front-facing camera, Retina Display, 8 to 64 GB storage |
| Gen 5 | October 2012 | Larger display, 16 to 64 GB storage |
| Gen 6 | July 2015 | 16 to 128 GB storage |
| Gen 7 | May 2019 | 32 to 256 GB storage | [...] Despite Apple's efforts, the decline of the iPod was all but assured. Smartphones offered more music playback functionality, and with the internet getting bigger and better, streaming services offered vast music libraries on demand. The result? A slow but steady decline in sales, and in September 2014, the unthinkable (but totally predictable) happened – Apple discontinued the classic iPod. title: Apple Kills iPod Nano and Shuffle
snippet:
In a show of its commitment to the iPod Touch, Apple doubled the storage capacity of its top-of-line model to 128 gigabytes. That version costs $300. An iPod Touch with 32 gigabytes of storage sells for $200.

The Nano and Shuffle came out in 2005 as less expensive and smaller alternatives to Apple’s standard iPod. The Cupertino, California, company stopped updating the Nano and Shuffle several years ago. [...] The company discontinued sales of the two music players Thursday in a move reflecting the waning popularity of the devices in an era when most people store or stream their tunes on smartphones.

The iPod product line still remains alive, though. Apple plans to continue selling its internet-connected iPod Touch.
